record_notes.DCP-LETT-1894: June 8, supplied 1856; seven body blocks, nine notes and bibliography read. Thanks missing intervening Layard letter, not his later reply or earlier Darwin 1794. Madagascar expedition conditional, future route in apparatus not completed present knowledge. Questions separate hybrid-cat fertility with parents/inter se, native dogs/wild crosses, mongrel uniformity, Ascension pigeon markings, short curled-tail greyhounds, Cape specimens and sea-bird identification books. P4 distinct Fry questions support later response, and P3 mongrel question matches surviving 1897 opening. No proof of receipt or replies to missing cat/cape questions.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1897: September–October 1856, incomplete opening/end; all five body blocks, seven notes, annotations and bibliography read. Exact range inferred from supposed overseas arrival of June 8 letter, not an independently documented arrival. Identity corroborated by exact Ascension and curled-tail questions; P1 opening directly discusses all shapes/colours in mongrel dogs in answer to P3 uniformity question. Telegony/impression anecdotes are Layard/Fry attributed reports, not experimentally established heredity. Mating preferences are Fry report. P4 cannot remember Ascension bars/rump, calls them Blue rocks without prior breed discrimination. P5 seen greyhound-like dog with slightly bushed curled tail, further inquiry and travel only planned. Handwritten Layard/Hybridity labels undated, not receipt dates.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2151: October 4, supplied 1857; four body blocks, eight footnotes, all five separately transcribed authorial enclosure questions and bibliography read. Ordered Smiters from Roe, uncertain Kinder/Trinder intermediary with segmented italic letters in raw display; do not silently identify a name. Asks Buckman to investigate, Holland fallback, cage display conditions and pure breeding; no actual results. Saw short Athenaeum abstract, requests full publication and earlier references, not completed reading of future report/offprint. Summary names Cnicus article but body concerns plant-culture report; do not substitute title. September account payment is distinct from present just ordered wording and not proof of specimen receipt. Five questions are actual Darwin enclosure, not the undated DAR47 annotation quoted in footnote8; latter excluded from export.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2177F: Supplied December 1, 1857 metadata record marked incomplete; preserved source fully inspected but no authentic body. Page explicitly says transcript not yet online, followed by editorial weeds summary. No footnote, scholarly section or bibliography. Treat body as unavailable despite extractor retaining availability message. October 4 to December 1 is not a one-day interval as one candidate line stated; neither elapsed time nor summary proves a Smiter/plant-report reply.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1794: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. December9,1855 complete seven-page ALS. Eight blocks, five footnotes and bibliography. Layard publications read, direct approach for information and long-bred Cape pigeon/duck/poultry skins contingent on available fanciers/time; old dying birds/bones specifications not collection completed. European breed loss/modification a hypothesis. Andersson account promised not received. P7–8 after closing are authorial continuation concerning Ceylon fanciers, proposed Thwaites approach and Benson uncertain shell locality. Benson memorandum1790P5–6 uniquely supports cross-correspondent use by December9; already known by December7 reply4354, so new witness does not move earliest known date later. Raw stemostoma here versus stenostoma in1790 preserved. Later books and December10 Thwaites approach remain future.

reading_method: Root independently read complete surviving new source bodies, metadata constraints, exclusions, footnotes, scholarly sections and bibliography. Actual special markup and figures inspected where present. Reused explicit accepted primary readings only after matching source and accepted evidence hashes. Historical decisions and notes are handwritten; validation packages evidence rather than adjudicating it.
